args.title: checkout-api: rolled back to v2.3.0 after v2.3.1 failed health checks in production
args.summary:
checkout-api v2.3.1 (deployed to all production regions: us-east, us-west, eu-west) failed health checks with error rate ~18% (0.18). Rolled back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production (v2.3.1-rc is staging-only and was unhealthy, so it was not a candidate).

Rollback detail: the first rollback attempt halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving the fleet mixed (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1). A retry completed the rollout; all three regions are now on v2.3.0 and the service is healthy with error rate ~0.2% (0.002).

No change-manager approval was required since v2.3.0 had previously been healthy in production. Follow-up: root-cause v2.3.1 and investigate the transient orchestrator error during the first rollback attempt.

trace.final:
Done. Summary:

**Rollback completed — checkout-api is healthy again**
- **Problem:** v2.3.1 was live in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), failing health checks at a ~18% error rate.
- **Target chosen:** **v2.3.0** — the most recent release that was previously healthy in production. (v2.3.1-rc is staging-only and itself unhealthy, so it was not eligible.)
- **Execution:** The first rollback halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving a mixed fleet (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on the bad v2.3.1). I retried and the rollout completed across all regions.
- **Verified:** All three regions now report v2.3.0, `healthy: true`, error rate 0.002 (~0.2%).

**Incident:** INC-0001 opened, SEV2, for checkout-api — on-call has been paged. Summary documents the failure, the rollback (including the transient partial-failure and retry), and follow-ups (root-cause v2.3.1, investigate the orchestrator error).

Note on approvals: no change-manager approval was needed, since the policy only requires it for deploying a version that has *never* been healthy in production — v2.3.0 had. The incident request timed out on the first attempt; I retried with the same idempotency key, and exactly one incident exists.
